newsitem.title: UK: UK gilt repo calms, 7.0 pct gilt 2002 loses lustre.
newsitem.headline: UK gilt repo calms, 7.0 pct gilt 2002 loses lustre.

text.p: The UK gilt repo market calmed on Friday after Thursday's hectic session and demand eased for the week's star performer -- the 7.0 percent gilt due 2002.

The first trade of the day on the gilt secured funds at just 1.5 percent, but the dealers said with supply now more evenly spread across the market the price soon edged up. It hit a high of 5.25 percent in early trade.
"It edged down again mid-morning but I don't think it's going to see the one percent area for a while," said one trader. It hit a low of 0.5 percent on Thursday.
He quoted the gilt at 2.0 percent at midday.
General collateral (GC) rates edged lower after the Bank of England forecast a shortage of just 650 million sterling. The market expected a much larger 900 million stg shortfall.

GC rates were quoted at 5.95 to 5.85 percent compared with 6.0 to 5.95 percent on Thursday. Further out, rates were steady at 6.0 to 5.90 percent for one week and 5.95 to 5.90 percent for one month GC.
The week's other special, the 6.0 percent gilt due 1999, also lost some of its value, especially at shorter maturities.
"There is really little value at all in the short-ated deals, but after two weeks it picks up a bit," said the trader.
He quoted the six percent gilt due 1999 at 5.5 percent in the shorter dates.
